title: Web Lead
text: ABOUT US At LangChain, our mission is to enable every company to own its intelligence. We believe agents will transform how companies operate, and we're building the foundation to make that future possible. Our open-source harnesses and LangSmith platform give developers and enterprises the infrastructure to run, improve, and govern agents at scale. We've raised $460M to date, with our most recent funding round valuing the company at $3B, backed by leading investors including Sequoia, Benchmark, IVP, and CapitalG. As we continue to expand our platform and tackle some of the hardest challenges in agent engineering, every team member has the opportunity to make a meaningful impact and help shape both our technology and the future of the industry. More than 7,000 organizations rely on LangSmith, from fast-growing startups to Fortune 500 enterprises, including NVIDIA, Bridgewater, LinkedIn, Workday, and Rippling. We're just getting started on making high-performing agents easier to build and manage at scale. ABOUT THE ROLE LangChain's web presence is both a product and a growth engine. Developers visit our site to evaluate our tools, learn what we build, and decide whether to go deeper. We're looking for a Web Lead to own the strategy, quality, and evolution of LangChain's web properties across marketing, product, and education. This is a high-ownership role for someone who thinks in systems and cares about craft. You'll set the strategic direction for how LangChain presents itself on the web, establishing the processes that keep the site accurate and high-performing, leading conversion and SEO initiatives, and partnering closely with content, design, growth engineering, and demand gen to bring it all together. WHAT YOU'LL DO Web Ownership - Lead the web roadmap. Maintain a clear, prioritized view of what needs to be built, fixed, or improved across LangChain's web properties, balancing strategic initiatives with ongoing maintenance, quality, and reliability. Translate business priorities into web plans and drive them to completion. - Coordinate cross-functional web work. Serve as the central point of contact for web across marketing, education, product marketing, design, and growth engineering. Run the intake, review, and launch process so teams can ship web changes with speed and confidence. - Own the site's structural health. Establish and enforce processes for keeping the site accurate, up-to-date, and free of technical debt. This includes governance for page creation and deprecation, content hygiene, and cross-functional intake so nothing slips through the cracks. - Manage the CMS and tooling stack. Own the relationship with our CMS and web tooling vendors. Ensure the right systems are in place for the team to operate efficiently, and evaluate new tools as the site's needs evolve. Conversion & Performance - Own conversion rate optimization. Develop and execute a CRO program across key pages, including homepage, product pages, pricing, and landing pages. Design and run experiments, analyze results, and translate findings into durable improvements to the site's ability to drive signups, product adoption, and pipeline. - Define and track web performance metrics. Establish the reporting framework for how we measure web effectiveness across traffic, engagement, conversion, and downstream impact on product metrics. Own a regular reporting cadence that gives stakeholders a clear view of what's working and where to invest. - Partner with demand gen on landing pages. Work closely with marketing to design, build, and optimize campaign landing pages that convert. Bring a disciplined, test-and-learn mindset to paid and organic landing page performance. SEO - Build the bridge between SEO and content. Partner with the content team to ensure editorial and technical content decisions are informed by search data, and that published content is positioned to capture and convert high-intent traffic. Establish shared processes for keyword research, on-page optimization, and performance tracking. - Partner with Content on SEO strategy for LangChain's web properties. Help define the organic search strategy across marketing and product pages, working in close partnership with our SEO agency and content team. Prioritize based on search intent, competitive opportunity, and business impact. - Own technical SEO. In partnership with engineering, ensure the site's technical foundation supports strong organic performance across site speed, Core Web Vitals, crawlability, schema markup, and indexing health. Strategy & Stakeholder Alignment - Be the strategic voice on web. Bring a clear point of view to questions like: what should the information architecture look like as we scale? How do we balance developer credibility with commercial clarity? How does the website evolve as the product and company grow? - Align web to business goals. Understand what marketing, sales, product, and education need from the site, and translate those needs into a coherent web strategy. WHAT YOU'LL BRING - Strategic operator. You can hold the long-term vision and the day-to-day execution at the same time. You know when to move fast and when to slow down and get alignment. - Deep web fluency. You understand how great websites are built; the architecture, the technical foundations, the tooling, and the operational discipline that drives performance. - Analytically rigorous. You know how to define what good looks like, instrument it, and use data to make decisions. You're comfortable in analytics platforms and can design and interpret experiments. - Developer audience instincts. You understand what earns trust with technical audiences and know how to present LangChain credibly to developers. - Collaborative and clear. You'll work across a lot of functions. You're able to build alignment, communicate trade-offs, and keep things moving without needing authority over everyone involved. COMPENSATION PHILOSOPHY We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks. We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations. BENEFITS Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible vacation, a 401(k) plan, meals on in-office days in the US and more.

Owns the software and agents behind outbound on every channel: inbound lead follow-up, prospecting, multi-channel sequences, email deliverability, calling and the quality of every message the agent writes, with people deciding what goes out. Serves Sales Development Representatives (SDRs), Account Executives (AEs), their managers and Marketing. The goal of the role is business impact for those teams: more positive replies, more meetings booked and more qualified pipeline for every dollar spent. Additionally, this role has a communication and evangelizing component: showing the teams it serves what works, and sharing content and open source projects with our developer community. This role suits an engineer who has already built agents or software for outbound and prospecting, such as sequencing, email deliverability, dialing or AI-written outreach. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Spends time with SDRs, AEs and their managers to find the prospecting work they repeat that the agent can take over. - Designs, builds and improves the agent's outbound workflows: what starts each run, what the agent reads and decides, what it drafts, and what waits for a rep's approval. - Builds the agentic system that follows up every inbound lead within minutes: it qualifies the lead, researches the person and the account, and drafts a first touch for the owner the routing rules assign. - Builds and improves the system that runs Marketing's outbound plays and campaigns for every rep, from the target list to the first touch. - Builds the software and agentic system behind multi-channel sequences, which combine email, LinkedIn and calls, choose each next touch from what the prospect did, and stop when the prospect replies on any channel. - Builds the email sending and deliverability system: sending domains and mailboxes, warm-up, daily limits, address checks, bounces, opt-outs and inbox placement across mail providers. - Builds the calling software reps use: call lists, dialing and the research a rep reads before each call. - Owns the quality of what the agent writes, so every message fits the prospect's signal, their history with us and the right product, and uses how much reps edit each message and the replies it gets to find what to fix. - Builds the safeguards that keep prospects from getting duplicate or overlapping outreach, and the sync that logs every email, LinkedIn action and call in Salesforce. - Builds experiments that test messages, channels, timing and sequences against held-out groups, measures which ones book meetings, and fixes or removes what doesn't. - Writes evals for every feature shipped, and ships each feature with its scorecard row. - Shows reps and their managers what works, and shares it through blog posts, webinars and open source. WHAT YOU'LL BRING - AI-Native Developer: You have a deep understanding of the LLM stack: prompting, retrieval (RAG), cognitive architectures, and agentic loops. You have likely already built with LangChain or LangGraph. - Engineering Foundation: You are a strong software engineer (typically 3+ years) with at least 1 year of experience specifically shipping LLM systems in production. - Self-Directed "Founder" Mentality: You don't need a ticket to tell you what to fix. You are comfortable navigating ambiguity, identifying high-impact problems, and driving them to completion autonomously. - Full-Stack Capability: Strong coding skills in Python or TypeScript (ideally both) and the ability to build end-to-end applications. - Customer-Centric: You enjoy the intersection of high-level engineering and direct customer impact. You can translate a customer's technical pain point into a scalable system architecture. NICE TO HAVES - Expertise with LangSmith for evaluation and monitoring. - Experience building or maintaining open-source projects. - A background in technical consulting, solutions engineering, or high-growth GTM teams. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage. The right person is opinionated about what good looks like and hands-on enough to help get there. WHAT YOU'LL DO COMMUNICATIONS - Define the themes and narratives LangChain is hitting. Spearhead the direction on what LangChain should be known for and translate that into a rolling communications strategy the whole team is working from. This is the backbone of everything else. - Own press and media relations. Kickstart our comms efforts, building and managing relationships with key journalists and outlets, drive proactive press coverage, and act as the point of contact for inbound media inquiries. - Shape executive visibility and thought leadership. Identify the moments, platforms, and formats where LangChain's leaders should have a voice, and help them show up with a clear, consistent point of view. - Lead announcement strategy. Plan and execute communications around major launches, funding, partnerships, and company milestones, working cross-functionally to make sure the story lands with the right audiences at the right time. - Set and uphold the communications standard. Define LangChain's voice in the outside world and the quality bar for anything that goes out under its name. BRAND - Shape brand direction in close partnership with the brand lead. The brand lead focuses on brand voice, visual identity, and standards. You'll work closely together to align on where the brand is headed, what it stands for, and how it shows up — with narrative and brand informing each other rather than operating separately. - Stay close to major brand moments. Bring a point of view on concept and messaging for out-of-home, awareness campaigns, and other brand initiatives. Work with the brand lead to make sure what we're saying and how we're showing up are pulling in the same direction. - Make sure brand and narrative feel like one thing. The brand should feel like a natural extension of the editorial point of view, and vice versa. SOCIAL & RICH MEDIA - Partner with the social lead on strategy, themes, and goals. The social lead focuses on growing LangChain's social channels and ways to amplify our content and messaging. Work together to ensure social is amplifying the themes and narratives the broader team is driving. - Shape LangChain's rich media approach together. Work with the social lead to develop a shared point of view on how video, audio, and other formats fit into the content mix — where they build audience, where they deepen credibility, and how to build the right execution muscle over time. - Track what's working, what's not, and use it to sharpen direction. Have a real point of view on what looks right, what earns trust with a technical audience, and where the work needs to go further. Give clear direction and help the designer do their best work. - Keep visual identity consistent across every channel. A media company looks like itself everywhere it shows up. ABOUT THE ROLE You'll join our GTM Systems team, which owns the systems LangChain's go-to-market actually runs on — Salesforce above all: the account and contact model, territory and routing, the sales process from first touch to closed-won, and the quote-to-cash and provisioning stack behind it. We design and ship internal product for the GTM organization. AI agents do a growing share of the building: they draft design docs, open changes, and run Salesforce deployments, while humans hold the approval gates. Build capacity — engineers plus the agent bench — sits on this team, and you'll help decide what it works on next. You'll own the requirements, prioritization, and quality bar for LangChain's Salesforce-centered GTM systems, turning ambiguous revenue-team needs into shipped process and systems changes that scale. This is not a ticket queue role. You'll be accountable for a small number of high-leverage GTM systems programs at a time: defining the problem, aligning stakeholders, specifying the solution, and ensuring what ships changes how the revenue org operates. You'll work across Sales, Marketing, Partnerships, Support, and Finance in a fast-changing environment where priorities move quickly and influence matters more than reporting lines. The core challenge is operating with authority but not control: aligning teams around tradeoffs as the business changes underneath the plan. You won't be expected to write production code. You will be expected to write clear enough specifications that engineers and AI coding agents can build from them, and to review the output with enough Salesforce and systems judgment to decide whether it is correct. Location: San Francisco Bay Area — in office 4 days a week. The people whose processes you're redesigning are in this building, and so are the engineers who build LangGraph. WHAT YOU'LL DO Carry multi-quarter programs - Own the Salesforce sales process from lead to close — routing, qualification, territory assignment, and stage progression — driving each initiative from discovery through UAT, change management, and adoption. - Be the person stakeholders come to before they file a request, especially when the system was never designed for what the business now needs. - Own the intake and prioritization model for hundreds of quarterly GTM systems requests, ensuring the team works on the highest-leverage business problems rather than the loudest tickets. Own what gets specified and what ships - Run discovery and turn ambiguous asks into BRDs, process flows, data models, and acceptance criteria — with a clear problem statement and ROI justification, precise enough to execute without a second conversation. - Hold the quality gate: you write the specification, engineers and coding agents write the code, and nothing reaches production without your sign-off. - Run vendor evaluations when the right answer is buy, integrate, or replace rather than build. Protect revenue data integrity - Trace anomalies in revenue fields — Net ARR, initial pipeline, lead source — back to the automation, trigger, or integration that wrote them. - Own the reconciliation seam between Salesforce, usage-based billing, and cloud-marketplace transactions. - Identify which design decisions are load-bearing and which are cosmetic, and catch the downstream failure modes before they reach production. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE: In your first 6–12 months, you might: - Redesign the lead-to-opportunity process so routing, qualification, and stage progression are measurable, enforceable, and adopted by the field. - Create a prioritization model for hundreds of GTM systems requests per quarter, with clear tradeoffs and business rationale. - Ship a Salesforce change that improves pipeline hygiene, quote-to-cash accuracy, provisioning reliability, or cloud marketplace reconciliation. - Establish a specification and UAT standard that engineers and AI agents can reliably build against. - Build enough trust with Sales, Marketing, Partnerships, Support, and Finance that stakeholders bring you the problem before they prescribe the solution. WHAT YOU'LL BRING SYSTEMS AND DOMAIN DEPTH - Domain and tenure — 6–8 years in business systems, sales systems, revenue systems, or GTM systems, with Salesforce as your primary platform throughout. - Sales process depth — you've partnered with Sales Ops on the things reps feel every day: territory and account coverage, lead qualification and routing, stage gates, and pipeline and forecast hygiene. - Sales systems / RevOps depth — experience across quote-to-cash, CPQ, territory and lead routing, forecasting, or adjacent revenue processes. - Technical fluency — you can read a data model, a Flow, and enough Apex to design against what's really there, even though you are not expected to write production code. PROGRAM LEADERSHIP - Program ownership — you've been the single accountable owner, at the working level negotiating the commitments yourself, of a program that spanned four or more functions and changed how a revenue org works day to day. - Release risk — you've delivered a program into a core system on a release process you didn't control, where another team's change could break your release. - Re-scoping under change — you've re-scoped a program mid-flight because the business changed under it, a sponsor moved, or the original scope no longer matched reality. - Holding the line — you've turned down a request with executive backing and kept the relationship; you hold the line when something breaks pricing discipline, a legal constraint, or the architecture, and you arrive with the alternative. JUDGMENT AND COMMUNICATION - One tradeoff, two audiences — you write for the reader in front of you, not the one you find easiest: the VP gets the page, the engineer gets the spec. - Maximum agency — you find the friction and start the project. You don't wait for a ticket. - AI judgment — you give an agent the same brief you'd give a new engineer, and you check its work the same way. - Architecture judgment — you know which design calls are load-bearing and which are cosmetic: why a usage event belongs on its own object rather than a field on Account, and how you'd catch that renaming one picklist breaks the provisioning saga before anyone deploys it. NICE TO HAVE'S None of these is a screen; any one makes you useful faster. - You've owned a core Salesforce object domain — Account, Contact, Lead, or Opportunity — through a full redesign. - You've traced a Salesforce field into a usage record into a provisioning step, and seen what broke downstream when it moved. - You've worked with cloud marketplace operations — AWS or GCP private offers, co-sell, entitlement mapping, metering, and the failure modes when they break. - You've worked with usage-based billing systems such as Metronome, Orb, or similar, and CRM↔billing identity reconciliation. - You have LangChain or LangGraph experience, or you're excited to learn it here from the people who build it. You’ll be equally deliberate about where humans remain essential: the conversations and strategic direction that enabling GTM at large requires. WHAT YOU’LL DO SET THE GLOBAL ENABLEMENT STRATEGY - Define and execute a GTM enablement strategy aligned with revenue growth, customer expansion, and market priorities. - Partner with executive and regional leaders to identify capability gaps and execution bottlenecks, directing investment toward the highest-impact opportunities. - Own enablement planning, budget, governance, and operating cadence, with clear priorities, ownership, and success measures across onboarding, technical and product enablement, and outbound enablement. - Decide where AI changes the enablement model and where human-led work stays, and set the standard the rest of GTM builds against. BUILD PROGRAMS THAT IMPROVE FIELD PERFORMANCE - Develop role-based enablement for Account Executives, Account Managers, Sales and Business Development Representatives, Partner/Channel Managers, Customer Engineering, and Deployed Engineering. - Tailor programs by segment, industry, and geography where it improves execution, preparing teams to support multiple use cases, buyer types, and platform opportunities. - Design and scale role-based 30/60/90-day onboarding that accelerates time to productivity and, for sellers, time to first deal. - Establish continuous learning, coaching, and certification programs that reinforce skills beyond onboarding. - Embed enterprise sales methodologies into day-to-day workflows, deal reviews, and pipeline inspections. - Equip frontline managers to reinforce skills, inspect execution, and coach consistently—making enablement part of how teams operate, not a separate training activity. - Structure programs so the knowledge behind them can be reused by AI-assisted practice, reinforcement, and certification, extending reach without proportional headcount. - Keep human coaching where it changes behavior, so scalable programs extend reach without replacing the conversations that build skill. HOW WE’LL MEASURE SUCCESS - Shorter time to full productivity across GTM roles and faster time to first deal for sellers. - Measurable contributions to improved win rates, average contract value, and pipeline velocity. - Consistent application of core sales methodologies, reinforced through frontline manager coaching and deal execution. - Demonstrated skill development and sustained behavior change—not just participation in training or adoption of tools. - Field readiness that keeps pace with product delivery and growing business complexity, with teams prepared to execute on new capabilities, use cases, and sales motions as they launch. - AI tools across GTM operating from one current knowledge base, with less rework, drift, and duplicated content, and less administrative work in delivery. - Broader enablement coverage at a lower cost per program, showing the field reached more often without proportional headcount. - Coaching quality as rated by managers and sellers, not just coaching activity. - Improved field and manager satisfaction with enablement, alongside positive trends in GTM team retention. You'll own order operations and billing configuration, working closely with Deal Strategy and Operations, Product, GTM Systems, Finance and Accounting, and Enterprise Engineering. Our bias is to invest in systems rather than in a growing queue of manual work, so you'll be setting the automation roadmap at the same time you're operating the function - deciding what a person should touch, what a workflow should handle, and what should never have been a step in the first place. Getting that right is what lets order volume grow by an order of magnitude without ops growing with it. This is a senior individual contributor role. You'll own order operations, working closely with Deal Strategy and Operations, GTM Systems, Finance and Accounting, and Enterprise Engineering. Those teams are your partners and much of your build capacity. Bringing them onto one shared order-to-cash roadmap is a core part of the job, and the reason we're hiring someone senior to do it. Bring the billing view into pricing and deal-structure decisions early, so new models and non-standard terms can be billed accurately and automated, not handled by hand - Set the automation roadmap. Instrument the path, put a number on every place a human touches an order, and decide what gets automated, what gets designed away, and what stays manual on purpose - Treat every billing error as a defect: find the root cause and fix the class of problem, not just the one invoice - Ship automations yourself where that's fastest, and partner with GTM Systems and Enterprise Engineering where the work belongs in core systems or the product - Write the playbook and the controls behind it: approvals, segregation of duties, reconciliations, and exception handling, built so order ops scales through systems rather than headcount and holds up under audit - Own three numbers and move them: touchless order rate, signature-to-provisioned cycle time, and billing accuracy WHAT YOU'LL BRING - 6+ years in order management, order-to-cash, billing operations, or revenue operations at a B2B SaaS company, including time building the function at an early-stage or fast-scaling one - Hands-on fluency with a modern billing and ERP stack. We run Salesforce, Metronome, and Rillet - you should know something comparable well enough to have opinions, and get to depth on ours quickly - Real experience with usage-based pricing. Per-seat is straightforward; metered consumption, commits, drawdowns, overages, and true-ups are where order ops gets interesting, and that's most of our business - Working knowledge of ASC 606 and month-end close. ABOUT THE ROLE We're hiring an Integrated Campaigns Manager to own how LangChain brings our biggest narratives to market through integrated, multi-channel campaigns and webinars programs that generate awareness, engagement, and pipeline globally. You'll partner closely with Product Marketing, Solutions, Industry Marketing, and Thought Leadership to translate messaging, customer stories, and content into full-funnel campaigns. From defining the campaign strategy and channel mix to building landing pages, launching webinars, coordinating promotion, and optimizing conversions, you'll own execution from start to finish. You'll be responsible for connecting the dots across channels, audiences, and regions, ensuring we're not just launching individual tactics but building cohesive campaigns that move prospects through the funnel. We're looking for someone who is equally comfortable developing a campaign strategy and getting into the details of execution. You should know how to turn an idea into a live campaign, measure what's working, and continuously optimize to drive pipeline. WHAT YOU'LL DO GLOBAL INTEGRATED CAMPAIGN STRATEGY AND PIPELINE - Build and own global integrated campaign plans across our core product, solutions, industry, and thought leadership narratives. - Partner with Product Marketing, Solutions, Industry Marketing, and Thought Leadership to translate positioning and content into campaigns with clear audiences, messaging, channels, and conversion goals. - Develop full-funnel campaign strategies that connect awareness and education to demand capture and pipeline generation. - Define campaign goals, audience segmentation, channel investments, and success metrics, with accountability for campaign-sourced and influenced pipeline. - Partner with regional demand generation and field marketing teams to adapt global campaigns for NAMER, EMEA, and APAC markets. - Build repeatable campaign playbooks and identify opportunities to scale successful programs across regions. END-TO-END CAMPAIGN EXECUTION You'll own the campaign from initial concept through launch, optimization, and reporting, and be hands-on throughout. - Integrated campaigns: Build and execute multi-channel campaigns across email, paid media, organic social, webinars, third-party promotion, and sales outreach. - Webinars and virtual programs: Own end-to-end webinar execution, including programming strategy, speaker coordination, promotional planning, registration and attendance optimization, and post-event follow-up. CROSS-FUNCTIONAL PARTNERSHIP - Work directly with Product Marketing and content marketing to understand product positioning, launches, and messaging priorities and translate them into global campaign strategies. - Identify compelling narratives, customer proof points, and campaign opportunities with cross-functional partners. - Partner with regional and field marketing teams to ensure global campaigns are relevant to local audiences and sales priorities. - Work closely with Performance Marketing, Lifecycle, and Marketing Ops to build coordinated programs across channels. - Collaborate with Sales and SDR teams on campaign activation, account targeting, and follow-up strategies that drive pipeline. - Own campaign planning, timelines, stakeholder alignment, and execution to ensure campaigns launch successfully. END-TO-END CAMPAIGN EXECUTION You'll own campaign execution across all three channels: - Google Ads: Build, launch, and manage campaigns across branded, non-branded, competitor, and product search, including keyword research, match types, negative keywords, bidding, and budget optimization. - Bing / Microsoft Advertising: Develop and manage campaigns tailored to Microsoft's search audience, identifying opportunities to extend reach and capture incremental high-intent demand. - ChatGPT advertising: Develop and execute an early advertising strategy, testing available placements, audience approaches, messaging, and conversion experiences as the platform evolves. - Creative and messaging: Write and test ad copy in partnership with Product Marketing, adapting messaging to each channel and its user intent. - Experimentation: Run structured tests to improve acquisition efficiency, traffic quality, and pipeline conversion. - Campaign operations: Own campaign setup, tracking validation, launch readiness, troubleshooting, and day-to-day optimization. MEASUREMENT, REPORTING, AND OPTIMIZATION - Own performance reporting across spend, traffic, conversions, qualified leads, meetings, opportunities, and pipeline. - Develop channel-specific measurement frameworks for Google Ads, Bing, and ChatGPT based on their available reporting and conversion capabilities. - Partner with Marketing Operations to connect advertising conversion signals with HubSpot and Salesforce data. - Optimize established search channels toward downstream pipeline signals, including offline conversion tracking where supported. - Establish a testing and measurement approach for emerging channels where attribution and optimization capabilities may be less mature. - Analyze performance across channels, audiences, campaigns, and landing pages to identify where to invest, optimize, or reduce spend. CROSS-FUNCTIONAL PARTNERSHIP - Partner with Product Marketing to translate positioning into search campaigns, AI advertising messaging, and landing page experiences. - Work closely with Web and Design on landing page development and conversion experimentation. - Collaborate with Marketing Operations on tracking, attribution, CRM integrations, and reporting accuracy. - Align with Demand Generation on product launches, campaign priorities, budget allocation, and pipeline targets. text: ABOUT US At LangChain, our mission is to make intelligent agents ubiquitous. We build the foundation for agent engineering in the real world, helping developers move from prototypes to production-ready AI agents that teams can rely on. We began as widely adopted open-source tools and have grown to also offer a platform for building, evaluating, deploying, and operating agents at scale. LangChain is a place where your contributions can shape how this technology shows up in the real world. Today, our platform includes LangSmith (Observability, Evaluation, Deployment, Fleet, and Sandboxes), our open source frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, and Deep Agents), and the newly launched LangSmith Engine for autonomous agent improvement. We have 100M+ monthly open source downloads, 6,000+ active LangSmith customers, and 5 of the Fortune 10 use LangSmith in production (+ 35% of the Fortune 500 overall), including teams at Klarna, Clay, Coinbase, Workday, Lyft, Cloudflare, Harvey, Rippling, Vanta, LinkedIn, Monday.com, Nvidia, and Bridgewater. About the Team The Python Open Source team maintains and evolves the core LangChain Python ecosystem used by millions of developers worldwide. We focus on building reliable, well-designed abstractions for developing AI agents and integrating them with real-world tools and systems. The team works closely with the open-source community, incorporating feedback and contributions while ensuring the core libraries remain stable, scalable, and production-ready. ABOUT THE ROLE We're looking for a Deployed Architect to join our Professional Services team. You'll work directly with enterprise customers to design, deploy, and optimize production-grade AI infrastructure and agent systems. You'll be responsible for architecting scalable, secure infrastructure deployments and building reliable, well-evaluated agent applications that solve real business problems. This role combines software development, infrastructure/platform engineering, and customer-facing skills. You'll work on everything from Kubernetes cluster design to multi-agent system architecture, requiring deep technical expertise across both infrastructure and agent engineering domains. This role offers direct impact on customer success, the opportunity to shape best practices, and work with cutting-edge AI technology. You'll join a collaborative team environment with a strong engineering culture. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES - Infrastructure & Platform Engineering: Design scalable, highly-available infrastructure for AI platform deployments (compute, storage, networking, security), enterprise integration patterns, Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Helm), multi-region HA/DR strategies, and CI/CD pipelines - Agent Engineering & Development: Design multi-agent systems using different patterns, implement agent logic using modern frameworks (langchain/langgraph), design comprehensive evaluation frameworks, optimize prompts with A/B testing, and guide deployment/operations - Customer Engagement & Assessment: Lead technical maturity assessments, work directly with enterprise customers to understand requirements and present recommendations, and partner with Engagement Managers and Product/Engineering teams WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR REQUIRED EXPERIENCE 7+ years of experience in a technical, hands-on customer-facing roles such as Solutions Architect or Forward Deployed Engineer. We also like former founders, so if you have an unusual background, but all the right skillsets, you are welcome to apply Infrastructure & Platform: - 3+ years of experience designing and deploying production infrastructure on cloud platforms (GCP, AWS, or Azure) - Strong Kubernetes experience (GKE, EKS, or AKS) including cluster design, autoscaling, and multi-zone deployments - Experience with Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Helm) and GitOps practices - Knowledge of database systems (relational databases, in-memory data stores) including HA, replication, backup strategies, and sizing - Experience designing high-availability and disaster recovery solutions - Strong understanding of networking, security (SSO/RBAC, TLS, secrets management), and observability (Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog) - Experience with CI/CD pipelines for infrastructure and applications Agent Engineering & Development: - 1+ years of experience building production AI/ML applications or agents - Strong experience with LLM frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, or similar) for building agent-based applications - Experience with state management patterns (short-term and long-term memory) - Experience designing and implementing evaluation frameworks for AI applications - Strong prompt engineering skills with experience in optimization and A/B testing - Experience with vector stores, RAG patterns, and knowledge organization - Experience with tool integration, API design, and error handling patterns - Strong Python and/or TypeScript development skills Customer-Facing: - Customer-facing experience with enterprise customers - Experience conducting technical assessments or infrastructure audits - Strong communication skills with ability to explain technical concepts to diverse audiences KEY ATTRIBUTES - Strong problem-solving skills with ability to analyze complex requirements and design elegant solutions - Excellent customer-facing communication skills, able to explain technical concepts to diverse audiences - Experience working cross-functionally with engineering teams, product teams, and customers - Consultative approach with ability to understand customer needs, provide recommendations, and guide implementation - Ability to balance infrastructure architecture with agent development work - Strong engineering background with hands-on development experience - Willing to travel up to 20% of the time Location: Remote Compensation: $170,000-$270,000 base salary + equity Looking to lead technical strategy across the customer journey from Proofs of Value (PoVs) to driving overall adoption? Please check out the Deployed Engineer listing focused on Account Strategy & Solutions. Compensation Philosophy: We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks. We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations. Drive performance investigations using memory and CPU profiling tools; own the path from profiling to shipped fix - Design and harden the distributed deployment of SmithDB services on Kubernetes (multi-tenant, high-throughput, low-latency) - Contribute to cloud object store integrations (S3, GCS, Azure Blob) and set the standard for how SmithDB manages data at rest and in flight - Build and maintain observability for the engine itself: metrics, tracing, debug tooling - Manage a small but growing team of systems engineers: set goals, run 1:1s, provide technical mentorship, and grow careers - Own the SmithDB technical roadmap in partnership with LangSmith product and engineering leadership - Communicate progress, risks, and tradeoffs clearly to the broader organization: you write concise, decision-ready updates What you'll bring - 7+ years in systems or database engineering, with at least 2 years in a technical lead or engineering management role - Experience building or contributing to columnar storage formats (Parquet, Arrow), OLAP query engines, or time-series stores - Background in observability infrastructure or tracing pipelines (OpenTelemetry, ClickHouse, Prometheus) - ABOUT THE ROLE: You'll own the requirements, prioritization, and quality bar for LangChain's Salesforce-centered GTM systems, turning ambiguous revenue-team needs into shipped process and systems changes that scale. This is not a ticket queue role. You'll be accountable for a small number of high-leverage GTM systems programs at a time: defining the problem, aligning stakeholders, specifying the solution, and ensuring what ships changes how the revenue org operates. You'll work across Sales, Marketing, Partnerships, Support, and Finance in a fast-changing environment where priorities move quickly and influence matters more than reporting lines. The core challenge is operating with authority but not control: aligning teams around tradeoffs as the business changes underneath the plan. You won't be expected to write production code. You will be expected to write clear enough specifications that engineers and AI coding agents can build from them, and to review the output with enough Salesforce and systems judgment to decide whether it is correct. Location: San Francisco Bay Area — in office 4 days a week. The people whose processes you're redesigning are in this building, and so are the engineers who build LangGraph. WHAT YOU'LL OWN: Carry multi-quarter programs - Own the Salesforce sales process from lead to close — routing, qualification, territory assignment, and stage progression — driving each initiative from discovery through UAT, change management, and adoption. - Be the person stakeholders come to before they file a request, especially when the system was never designed for what the business now needs. - Own the intake and prioritization model for hundreds of quarterly GTM systems requests, ensuring the team works on the highest-leverage business problems rather than the loudest tickets. Own what gets specified and what ships - Run discovery and turn ambiguous asks into BRDs, process flows, data models, and acceptance criteria — with a clear problem statement and ROI justification, precise enough to execute without a second conversation. - Hold the quality gate: you write the specification, engineers and coding agents write the code, and nothing reaches production without your sign-off. - Run vendor evaluations when the right answer is buy, integrate, or replace rather than build. Protect revenue data integrity - Trace anomalies in revenue fields — Net ARR, initial pipeline, lead source — back to the automation, trigger, or integration that wrote them. - Own the reconciliation seam between Salesforce, usage-based billing, and cloud-marketplace transactions. - Identify which design decisions are load-bearing and which are cosmetic, and catch the downstream failure modes before they reach production. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE: In your first 6–12 months, you might: - Redesign the lead-to-opportunity process so routing, qualification, and stage progression are measurable, enforceable, and adopted by the field. - Create a prioritization model for hundreds of GTM systems requests per quarter, with clear tradeoffs and business rationale. - Ship a Salesforce change that improves pipeline hygiene, quote-to-cash accuracy, provisioning reliability, or cloud marketplace reconciliation. - Establish a specification and UAT standard that engineers and AI agents can reliably build against. - Build enough trust with Sales, Marketing, Partnerships, Support, and Finance that stakeholders bring you the problem before they prescribe the solution. WHAT YOU'LL NEED TO BE SUCCESSFUL: SYSTEMS AND DOMAIN DEPTH - Domain and tenure — 6–8 years in business systems, sales systems, revenue systems, or GTM systems, with Salesforce as your primary platform throughout. - Sales process depth — you've partnered with Sales Ops on the things reps feel every day: territory and account coverage, lead qualification and routing, stage gates, and pipeline and forecast hygiene. - Sales systems / RevOps depth — experience across quote-to-cash, CPQ, territory and lead routing, forecasting, or adjacent revenue processes. - Technical fluency — you can read a data model, a Flow, and enough Apex to design against what's really there, even though you are not expected to write production code. PROGRAM LEADERSHIP - Program ownership — you've been the single accountable owner, at the working level negotiating the commitments yourself, of a program that spanned four or more functions and changed how a revenue org works day to day. - Release risk — you've delivered a program into a core system on a release process you didn't control, where another team's change could break your release. - Re-scoping under change — you've re-scoped a program mid-flight because the business changed under it, a sponsor moved, or the original scope no longer matched reality. - Holding the line — you've turned down a request with executive backing and kept the relationship; you hold the line when something breaks pricing discipline, a legal constraint, or the architecture, and you arrive with the alternative. JUDGMENT AND COMMUNICATION - One tradeoff, two audiences — you write for the reader in front of you, not the one you find easiest: the VP gets the page, the engineer gets the spec. - Maximum agency — you find the friction and start the project. You don't wait for a ticket. - AI judgment — you give an agent the same brief you'd give a new engineer, and you check its work the same way. - Architecture judgment — you know which design calls are load-bearing and which are cosmetic: why a usage event belongs on its own object rather than a field on Account, and how you'd catch that renaming one picklist breaks the provisioning saga before anyone deploys it. ABOUT THE ROLE The ways customers buy from us are multiplying as fast as the business is growing. Enterprise order forms. Private offers through AWS, GCP, and Azure. A self-serve business running on usage-based pricing, with commits, drawdowns, and true-ups behind it. Each one is a distinct path from signature to cash, and each one runs today on some mix of manual steps and automation that grew up with the business. This role owns what comes next. You'll run order operations end to end - booking, provisioning, invoicing, amendments, and renewals - on a stack we picked deliberately and recently: Salesforce, Metronome for metering and billing, Rillet for ERP. The stack is modern, but the processes on top of it were built to keep up with growth, not designed to scale. Your job is to decide what each one should become: keep it, rebuild it, automate it, or retire it. Our bias is to invest in systems rather than in a growing queue of manual work, so you'll be setting the automation roadmap at the same time you're operating the function - deciding what a person should touch, what a workflow should handle, and what should never have been a step in the first place. Getting that right is what lets order volume grow by an order of magnitude without ops growing with it. This is a senior individual contributor role. You'll own order operations, working closely with Deal Strategy and Operations, GTM Systems, Finance and Accounting, and Enterprise Engineering. Those teams are your partners and much of your build capacity. Bringing them onto one shared order-to-cash roadmap is a core part of the job, and the reason we're hiring someone senior to do it. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own the order-to-cash path end to end: order form intake from Deal Desk, booking in Salesforce, plan and entitlement setup in Metronome, invoicing and revenue recognition through Rillet, and the amendments, true-ups, and renewals that follow - Build out cloud marketplace operations across AWS, GCP, and Azure: private offer setup, usage reporting to each marketplace, and reconciling marketplace disbursements back to what we billed. Every new channel launches against defined readiness criteria, so marketplace deals run on the same clean path as direct ones - Own self-serve billing operations: usage metering, plan changes, dunning, credits, rebills, refunds, and the escalations behind them - Own billing and usage completeness at month-end close. Every order, credit, and metered event is reconciled between Metronome and Rillet before revenue is recognized, not after - Partner with Deal Strategy and Product as our pricing evolves. Bring the billing view into pricing and deal-structure decisions early, so new models and non-standard terms can be billed accurately and automated, not handled by hand - Set the automation roadmap. Instrument the path, put a number on every place a human touches an order, and decide what gets automated, what gets designed away, and what stays manual on purpose - Treat every billing error as a defect: find the root cause and fix the class of problem, not just the one invoice - Ship automations yourself where that's fastest, and partner with GTM Systems and Enterprise Engineering where the work belongs in core systems or the product - Write the playbook and the controls behind it: approvals, segregation of duties, reconciliations, and exception handling, built so order ops scales through systems rather than headcount and holds up under audit - Own three numbers and move them: touchless order rate, signature-to-provisioned cycle time, and billing accuracy WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 6+ years in order management, order-to-cash, billing operations, or revenue operations at a B2B SaaS company, including time building the function at an early-stage or fast-scaling one - Hands-on fluency with a modern billing and ERP stack. We run Salesforce, Metronome, and Rillet - you should know something comparable well enough to have opinions, and get to depth on ours quickly - Real experience with usage-based pricing. Per-seat is straightforward; metered consumption, commits, drawdowns, overages, and true-ups are where order ops gets interesting, and that's most of our business - Working knowledge of ASC 606 and month-end close. You don't need to be an accountant, but you should know what Revenue Accounting needs from billing data and why - Cloud marketplace experience (AWS, GCP, or Azure private offers), or a track record of getting deep on a system like that fast - A history of automating your own job. We'll ask you to walk us through a manual process you deleted: what it cost before, what you built, and what it costs now - The ability to build alignment across teams with different priorities and get to a decision, without relying on org authority - Comfort shipping a v0 earlier than feels comfortable, then iterating with real feedback NICE TO HAVE - SQL, Python, or low-code tooling in your own hands rather than on someone else's backlog - Experience building agents or LLM workflows for internal operations. We'd like to run more of our own back office on the LangSmith Platform, wherever it's the right tool and meets the same accuracy bar as the rest of order-to-cash - Audit prep or SOX readiness experience Compensation: $155,000 - $185,000 salary + options Compensation Philosophy: We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks. We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. text: At Composio, we are building infrastructure that allows agents to communicate with the tools you use for work including Github, Gmail, Notion, Salesforce, etc. We are a small team of engineers wrangling problems from context to search, that help us provide the most capable bridge between your agents and your tools. We raised a $25M Series A from Lightspeed https://lsvp.com/stories/investing-in-composio-building-the-backbone-of-ai-agent-intelligence/ with angels like Guillermo Rauch (CEO of Vercel), Dharmesh Shah (CTO of Hubspot), and Gokul Rajaram. We've 3x'd our ARR this year, and our customers range from your friends in the YC batch to Wabi, Glean, Zoom and many more. running stateful agent infrastructure inside someone else's cluster is new territory. this role defines what reliable, repeatable on-prem agent deployment looks like, across the customers running us in their own environments. THE FRONTIER YOU'LL WORK ON • fleet-managing agent runtimes across air-gapped, regulated, BYOK environments has no playbook. you define one. • turning hand-managed on-prem deployments into a repeatable product. the difference between 5 self-hosted customers and 50. • every incident, CVE, and upgrade wave here is unsolved at the ecosystem level. your runbooks lead the industry. WHAT YOU'LL DO? • own the on-prem lifecycle: helm charts, upgrades, the weekly release train, rollback paths. • drive chart convergence: diverged customer forks back onto one supported chart, with guardrails. • build structured onboarding (replicated or equivalent) so a new customer deploys in days, not weeks. • debug across the stack: temporal workflows, k8s init ordering, storage backends, auth-refresh pipelines. • own the security surface: CVE triage, patching, RCAs, bulletins. keep customers running when releases freeze. • co-own per-customer tool patching with the platform team. • dogfood Composio on your own deployment and support workflows. OPTIONAL • temporal, Postgres, cloud secret managers (GCP / AWS). • replicated or packaged self-hosted delivery (kots, airgap bundles). • compliance: SOC 2, Vanta-style programs, security questionnaires. • major open source contributions.

title: Growth and Data Engineer
text: At Composio, we are building infrastructure that allows agents to communicate with the tools you use for work including Github, Gmail, Notion, Salesforce, etc. We are a small team of engineers wrangling problems from context to search, that help us provide the most capable bridge between your agents and your tools. We raised a $25M Series A from Lightspeed https://lsvp.com/stories/investing-in-composio-building-the-backbone-of-ai-agent-intelligence/ with some incredible angels like Guillermo Rauch (CEO of Vercel), Dharmesh Shah (CTO of Hubspot), Gokul Rajaram. Beginning of this year we 3x our ARR, our customers range from your friends in the YC batch to Wabi, Glean, Zoom and many more. Our product is used by prosumers (MCP / CLI), developers (SDK), and enterprises. The job of the growth team is to increase usage and revenue across all three products. We accomplish this with a ruthless focus on analytics to inform the products we ship, features we highlight, and leads we hand off to sales. We're looking to hire a talented engineer who is as comfortable in SQL as they are in nextJS - someone who's excited to own the analytics foundations of the company and use it to drive our next phase of growth. WHAT YOU'LL DO? - Own our data foundation. Build and run the data lake and analytics stack that ties together all three products - MCP/CLI, SDK, and enterprise. You'll own Snowflake end to end: building pipelines, modeling clean generated tables, keeping the data trustworthy, and being the person who can answer the questions nobody else can. - Turn behavior into decisions. Dig into how people actually use Composio, chase down the trickiest analytics questions, and translate what you find into roadmap calls - what to double down on, what to kill, and what deserves the next bet. This work directly guides where product invests. - Build the product-led sales engine. Instrument our funnels and flag PLS signals into Snowflake so consumer and developer usage becomes a clean, agile handoff to sales. Connecting a prosumer's MCP usage or a developer's SDK adoption to the right enterprise conversation is core to how we grow. - Ship growth features in the product. You're as comfortable in Next.js as in SQL. You'll build in-product upsells, sharpen onboarding and ship new onboarding flows, and drive in-app actions like booking a sales meeting - without ever making it feel bolted on. The experience stays delightful. - Own activation and retention. Run email activation and reactivation campaigns, close funnel gaps, and take these problems from goal to shipped without waiting for a PM to turn them into tickets. - Scope ruthlessly. Ship the narrow, signal-generating version today, read the data, then either kill the idea or build it properly. - Work across the company. Partner with product, sales, marketing, and engineering to turn distribution ideas into shipped product. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR The data instinct is the part that's hard to teach. Strong engineers can round out the rest quickly, so we weight it accordingly. - Data fluency (non-negotiable). You write SQL fluently, are at home living in a warehouse like Snowflake, and can model data, stand up tracking, build dashboards, and reason clearly from messy funnel data. You're genuinely curious about user behavior and driven to answer the hardest questions. This is the heart of the role. - Strong engineer. You ship polished frontend and backend systems and context-switch across codebases without losing speed. If your product-engineering chops are still catching up to your data ability, that's fine - we'd rather hire a great data mind who's hungry to round out the full stack than the reverse. - Growth taste. You know the difference between a cheap experiment and a sloppy product, and you'd rather ship a narrow signal-generating version today than a perfect unknown next week. - AI-native. You build with LLMs and keep up with what's happening in the ecosystem. - Owner. You take a goal, decide what to build, ship it, measure whether it worked, and flex across all of the above. - Human. You build trust and admit what you don't know. STRONG PREFERENCE FOR - Hands-on experience with Snowflake (or a comparable warehouse) in production — modeling, pipelines, and performance - Fluency with Next.js and modern full-stack web development - Prior growth or product engineering at a startup BONUS POINTS - You've built something that got real traction - A presence in the AI community through open source, writing, or building in public - Interest in owning performance marketing and media mix modeling — measuring and disentangling what's actually driving growth across channels

title: Solutions Architect
text: SOLUTIONS ARCHITECT, COMPOSIO San Francisco, in office · Full-time An agent is only useful when it can act. It has to read the inbox, update the CRM, open the pull request and file the ticket, on the right user's account, with the right permissions. Most agents still cannot do this reliably in production. Composio is the action layer that makes it work. We connect agents to 1,500+ apps, with managed authentication, tool definitions models can use, and the controls an enterprise needs before it lets an agent near real data. Developers reach us through our SDK, MCP and the MCP Gateway. WHY COMPOSIO - Traction. We serve more than 1B tool calls a month, and we have tripled our ARR since the start of this year. - Customers. They range from early-stage YC companies to Wabi, Glean and Zoom. - Backing. We raised a $25M Series A led by Lightspeed, with angel investors including Guillermo Rauch (CEO, Vercel), Dharmesh Shah (CTO, HubSpot) and Gokul Rajaram. - Team. We are a small team of engineers working on hard problems, from context to search, and we ship fast. THE ROLE This is not a demo role. As Solutions Architect, you are the technical owner of deals with developer-led companies and enterprises investing in agents. You walk into a customer, learn how their identity, data, apps and governance fit together, and design an architecture that survives their security review. You build the proof of concept yourself, and you hand a working deployment to our forward deployed engineers after close. Customers should come to see you as an adviser on how to move their agents from proof of concept to production, not as a vendor. WHAT YOU WILL DO - Own the technical win. Partner with our account executives to lead discovery and evaluation with heads of AI, CTOs and architects. - Design the architecture. Decide how a customer's agents connect to their apps: SDK, MCP or MCP Gateway; managed or custom OAuth; cloud, VPC or self-hosted. - Build the proof. Build proofs of concept end to end in TypeScript or Python, against the customer's real apps. - Clear security review. Work through token custody, data flow, SSO/SCIM and audit logs with platform, identity and security teams. - Build for the team. Create demos, reference architectures and sample agents that the wider sales team can reuse. - Close the loop with the product. Bring repeated customer problems to product and engineering when they should become platform features. If a small fix will unblock a deal, ship it yourself. WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR - 4+ years in solutions engineering, solutions architecture, forward deployed engineering or software engineering, ideally at a developer tools, infrastructure or AI company. - Applied engineering. You ship production TypeScript or Python - AI-native. You build with Claude Code, Codex or Cursor every day, you have shipped an agent that calls real tools on real accounts. - API and authentication depth. You understand auth in detail - OAuth 2.0, SAML, SCIM, SSO. - Enterprise experience. You have taken a technical evaluation through security review, and you work as well with a staff engineer as with a CIO. - Clear communication. You write precise architecture documents and prompt follow-ups, and you explain complex products simply, to engineers and executives alike. - Ownership and urgency. You are comfortable where the playbook is still being written, and you create structure without waiting for it. - Trustworthiness. You build trust with customers, ask direct questions, admit what you do not know, and follow through. COMING FROM A DIFFERENT BACKGROUND? Solutions engineering is one path into this role, not the only one. If one of these describes you, we want to talk: - Agent builder. You have built agents with the Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, LangGraph, Mastra or similar, and you have felt the pain of giving them access to real apps. - Backend engineer. You have shipped and run production services, and you know what it takes to observe and scale them. - Identity and security engineer. You know OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, SCIM and token lifecycles in depth. - Integration engineer. You have connected enterprise systems with iPaaS, ETL or API gateways, and you see tool calling as the next version of that work. - Founder. You have built a developer product and sold it to technical buyers yourself.

title: Member Technical Staff - Applied AI Engineer (US Timing)
text: Member of Technical Staff – Applied AI Engineering EXPERIENCE: 2–4 years TYPE: Full-time FOCUS: Applied AI Customer-facing WORK HOURS: US Timings LOCATION: Bengaluru ABOUT THE COMPANY At Composio, we are building infrastructure that allows AI agents to communicate with the tools people use for work, including GitHub, Gmail, Notion, Salesforce, and more. We are a small team of engineers working across context, auth, execution, and reliability to build the action layer for AI agents. We raised a $25M Series A from Lightspeed, with angel investors including Guillermo Rauch (CEO of Vercel), Dharmesh Shah (CTO of HubSpot), and Gokul Rajaram. Our customers range from YC startups to companies like Brex, Glean, Zoom, and more. ABOUT THE TEAM This is an applied AI engineering role, not a traditional support role. You will work directly with customers, learn the repeated work behind their problems, and build agentic systems that take that work over. When a customer needs direct engineering, you will debug and ship. When a pattern repeats, you will turn it into a workflow, eval, tool, or product capability that compounds. • The frontier: support is one of the richest applied AI environments — an agent has to gather context, reason across systems, use tools, take bounded action, verify the outcome, and communicate clearly. You design that system. • The trust bar: AI cannot be trusted by default with customer support. You define state, permissions, guardrails, evals, and escalation paths so the automation earns trust. • The feedback loop: it's immediate. Deploy into real support work, watch where the system fails, and improve it until people can hand over more of the job. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES What you'll build • Agentic workflows that take over support functions: intake, classification, context gathering, reproduction, diagnosis, response drafting, remediation, verification, and follow-up. • Tool-using agents that safely inspect runs, logs, auth state, configuration, and provider behavior, then propose or execute bounded recovery actions. • Eval suites for diagnostic correctness, resolution quality, safe escalation, customer communication, and end-to-end task completion. • Human-in-the-loop systems that make ownership, uncertainty, approvals, handoffs, and failure states explicit. • The observability, memory, and feedback loops that let these agents improve from real support cases without repeating mistakes. • Product improvements that remove entire classes of customer issues instead of handling the same symptoms faster. How you'll work • Start with the customer outcome, then work backward into the model, workflow, tooling, or product change required to deliver it. • Own the hardest issues end to end when direct engineering is needed: reproduce, isolate, mitigate, ship, communicate, and verify the resolution with the customer. • Sit with customers and partner with Support, FDE, Product, and Engineering to find work that should become software. • Move from a rough prototype to a reliable production workflow, with traces, evals, guardrails, and a clear human fallback. • Use frontier models, coding agents, and internal AI tools every day to multiply your own engineering output. • Measure success in customer outcomes improved, support work removed, and classes of failure prevented. text: ENGINEERING SUPPORT LEAD Location: San Francisco · Full time ABOUT COMPOSIO Composio builds the AI-native automation layer for software teams: SDKs, runtimes, and platform tooling that let developers compose, evaluate, and operate agentic workflows and AI-powered products. You will build the coverage, handoffs, coaching, and escalation paths that make the experience consistent for customers and sustainable for the team. Review case quality, unresolved work, customer outcomes, and the reasons customers contact us again. - Hire, onboard, and coach technical support engineers. Run case reviews, give direct feedback, and create paths for people to grow in support and engineering-adjacent work. - Bring AI into the daily support workflow. Use Composio and work with our applied AI engineers to improve intake, context gathering, investigation, drafting, and follow-up; measure quality and keep clear human ownership when a workflow fails. - Build a demand and capacity view that informs staffing and coverage decisions before the queue falls behind. - Work with FDE, Product, and Engineering to turn patterns in customer cases into product fixes, self-serve guidance, and better developer experience. Prior experience supporting an AI product is useful. What matters most is proven ownership in support and the drive to build a better support organization with AI.

title: APM - integrations
text: WHO ARE WE? Composio builds the AI-native automation layer for software teams: SDKs, runtimes, and platform tooling that let developers compose, evaluate, and operate agentic workflows and AI-powered products. Our systems must be reliable at scale - agents must act correctly, integrations must be robust, and integration needs to be an autonomous, observable function that accelerates engineering rather than slowing it. You'll join a small, high-leverage team building the delivery systems and metrics that give product and support teams visibility and predictable delivery. This role is based in Bangalore (HSR). WHO IS OUR IDEAL CANDIDATE? A high-agency operator who is also AI-native, and who wants to grow into product. The role starts ops-heavy: you run the operations that get apps live on Composio, keep the toolkits healthy, and automate as much of that work as you can. Over 6-8 months, once those workflows and automations are running, the role shifts towards owning ambiguous product problems across the platform - triggers, tools, skills, auth, governance, and toolkit-level issues like rate limits and MCP hosting. This is not a traditional PM role with an engineering team to direct. It's closer to founder-mode ownership of a product line, where you solve problems using agents and a small ops team. You've shipped things on your own - a side project, a tool, a micro-business, or a system you built that is still running - and you've run real operations with quality bars, not just executed inside someone else's process. You're at the edge of AI out of genuine curiosity: you use AI tools daily and can point to specific things you built or automated with them in the last month. You pick work by impact, not by how interesting it is, and you have no ego about manual work that isn't automated yet. You can hold a technical conversation with engineers without a translator, and you're comfortable owning problems that don't have a clear owner yet. WHAT WILL THEY OWN? - The toolkit number: how many apps are live on Composio, and the health of the ones already live. - New apps, end to end: run the operations of getting them live - research, setup, QA, launch. - Existing toolkits: make them better with the product team, and clear the issues that stop them from working well. - QA and support for every toolkit you bring live. Once it's live, its quality is your problem. - The ops playbook: build it, run it, scale it. SOPs, small tools, AI agents before humans - you automate yourself first, and when scaling takes people, hiring them is part of the job. - The metrics for this function: define them, build them, watch them. - Product problems, as the ops layer starts running on its own: ambiguous, non-engineering problems across triggers, tools, auth, governance and toolkit-level issues - scoped, owned and shipped by you. WHAT ARE WE LOOKING FOR? - Experience: 2-4 years. We care more about how fast you've grown than how senior you are. - Technical floor: can explain what an API and an integration are, reads API docs cold, writes enough code to build small tools and automations. Not an engineer; infra-level work is not the job. - AI-native automation instinct: your default answer to repeated work is "how do I never do this manually again" - backed by recent, specific evidence of things you've built or automated with AI. - Dirty-work appetite: you happily run the manual version today while the automation is being built. This and the automation instinct are both required; we never average them. - Process maturity: you've designed or owned a pipeline with throughput, SLAs, or quality bars, and you left systems running behind you - not just stories. - Product instinct: you can take a vague problem, figure out what's actually broken, and decide what to build or fix - without waiting for a spec or a dedicated engineering team. - Organized ownership: routines, follow-ups, nothing dropped. You communicate clearly, in writing and in person. - High agency in uncertainty: given a goal with no playbook and no owner above you, you define the problem yourself and start before permission. - Operating maturity: this role carries a number from week one, so it needs someone who has owned outcomes before. It is not internship-shaped. We'll pass at any stage on candidates who only want the cool parts of the job, choose work by interestingness over impact, can't explain what an API is, or do the same manual work in month three as month one. NICE-TO-HAVE - Founder or early-stage experience: you've taken something from zero, or joined early and owned a function. - Experience with SaaS integrations, API products, or developer-facing products. - Built things with agents or LLM workflows beyond personal use - tools, experiment logs, side projects other people use. - An engineering-adjacent path: studied engineering and moved into non-technical work, or a non-CS background with things you built on the side. - High-throughput ops backgrounds (delivery, marketplace, physical ops) count only alongside the AI-native bar above - on their own they are not this job. OUTCOMES WE EXPECT IN THE FIRST 90 DAYS - More toolkits live on Composio - you own the supply number, and it moved. - Existing toolkits repaired or unblocked without anything breaking technically. - A v1 ops playbook running: SOPs, automations, and AI agents handling the repeatable parts of onboarding and QA. - Metrics for the function defined and visible: supply, health of supply, pipeline status. - What this is not: usage. Usage is a product metric; this role is measured on supply and the health of supply.

title: Research Engineer / Scientist, Post-Training
text: SOLVING SELF-IMPROVING SUPERINTELLIGENCE The human brain is a sponge. Today’s AI brains are brittle and rigid. At Letta, we’re building self-improving artificial intelligence: creating agents that continually learn from experience and adapt over time. Founded by the creators of MemGPT from UC Berkeley’s Sky Computing Lab (the birthplace of Spark and Ray). Backed by Jeff Dean, Clem Delangue, and pioneers across AI infrastructure. Our agents already power production systems at companies like 11x https://www.letta.com/case-studies/11x and Bilt Rewards https://www.letta.com/case-studies/bilt, learning and improving every day. We’re assembling a world-class team of researchers and engineers to solve AI’s hardest problem: making machines that can reason, remember, and learn the way humans do. Note that this role is in-person (no hybrid), 5 days a week in downtown San Francisco. YOUR ROLE You will pioneer post-training techniques that improve how well LLMs can be integrated into complete agentic systems. At Letta, you'll work with a world-class, tight-knit team of AI researchers and engineers towards our vision of self-improving superintelligence. Advance the field through open publishing of research through papers, technical reports, blog posts, and open-source code. WHAT YOU’RE RESPONSIBLE FOR: - Training models for better agentic tool-use, particularly for context management - Designing mechanisms for continuous model weight updates post-deployment without catastrophic forgetting - Designing and run experiments to improve understanding of the interplay between data mixtures, training algorithms, and models - Building infrastructure for generating and collecting synthetic data at scale - Building challenging evals for measuring agentic capabilities WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR: - Proficiency in python and deep learning frameworks eg. PyTorch - Expertise in post-training techniques e.g. SFT fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, reward models, preference learning - Ability to balance execution speed with empirical rigor - Proven track record of impactful research (breakthrough publications and/or open-source contributions) - Real-world impact beyond pure academic work OUR CULTURE SIGNS IT COULD BE A GREAT FIT: - You want to maximize your impact: you want work on a small, incredibly talented team where every individual plays a huge role in the team's success. You wonder what it would have been like to be at OpenAI when it was just a dozen people, or Google when it was just a couple of grad students in a garage. - You’re excited to go head-to-head with tech giants, frontier labs, and other startups that are many times our size in both headcount and funding. - You are fundamentally opposed to closed frontier AI that is controlled by a handful of billionaires and private tech companies. SIGNS IT’S A BAD FIT: - You like stability, and get stressed out when there’s nobody telling you exactly what to do. We look for people that thrive in ambiguity and can intuit the most important problems by talking to customers and dogfooding our product. - You want to work a 9-5, and value clear separation of work from life. The stakes are the highest they've ever been, and the only moat is execution velocity. Operating on a strict 9-5 guarantees failure. - You value titles or want to people-manage. Letta is a flat company where every researcher and engineer is an individual contributor. OUR INTERVIEW PROCESS: - Initial screen (30 min) - Technical screen (1-1.5 hours) - Paid in-person work trial (2 days onsite in SF)

title: Member of Technical Staff - Systems
text: ABOUT US: AI NEEDS A NEW INFRASTRUCTURE LAYER. WE'RE BUILDING IT AT MODAL. Every era of computing brought new workloads that previous infrastructure couldn't support: mainframes, databases, and the cloud. Each time, the company that rebuilt the layer underneath defined the decade. AI is no different, except it touches everything instead of one slice, and the window to build the layer underneath it is open right now. Our customers include category-defining companies like Ramp https://modal.com/blog/how-ramp-built-a-full-context-background-coding-agent-on-modal, Cognition, DoorDash, and Suno. They rely on Modal for instant GPU access, sub-second container starts, and native storage, so it's simple to serve low-latency inference, fine-tune models, and access production-ready sandboxes at scale. We've passed $1B in annualized run rate, up 15x from a year ago. In October 2026 we raised a $750M Series D led by Accel at a $15.75B valuation. Our team includes creators of popular open-source projects (e.g., Seaborn https://github.com/mwaskom/seaborn, Luigi https://github.com/spotify/luigi), academic researchers, international olympiad medalists, and experienced engineering and product leaders with decades of experience. THE ROLE: We are looking for strong engineers with experience and interest in designing, building, and maintaining the novel, high-performance systems that make up our serverless platform. YOU MAY BE A FIT IF: - You have 5+ years of experience writing high-quality production code - You’ve built high-performance distributed systems at a large scale (the more battle scars, the better) - You have strong cloud skills - You have strong knowledge of low-level operating system foundations (Linux kernel, file systems, containers, etc.) - You have experience with performance engineering (tell us a story of when you shaved off a few milliseconds!) - You’re able to work in person in our NYC or SF office - You’re able to participate in our on-call rotation and respond to production incidents NICE-TO-HAVE: - Prior experience with Rust

We’re building a platform that covers the whole life of an LLM (train it, deploy it, observe it), and inference is where teams feel the difference every day.
